rule: When recapturing, pick the piece that keeps my queen and rooks off squares one enemy knight jump can fork, e.g. Rxe3? Nd5 hits Qc3+Re3.
trigger: I can capture an enemy piece on my 2nd or 3rd rank with my queen or a rook, and an enemy knight is one jump from where it could attack two of my queen, rooks or king after the recapture.
check: After my capture, can an enemy knight jump to a square attacking my queen and a rook (or king) together? If yes, recapture with the other piece or move one of them off that pattern.

rule: Before moving my king, keep it guarding nearby pawns an enemy knight could capture with check, e.g. Kh1 dropping g3.
trigger: An enemy knight is near my king, and my king is the only defender of a pawn beside it on my 2nd or 3rd rank.
check: After my king move, can an enemy knight capture a pawn my king stopped guarding, or land with check? If yes, choose a different king square or defend that pawn first.

rule: When an enemy pawn or knight chases my bishop back with tempo, set TREND worse and seek a central pawn break or a trade.
trigger: In my last few moves one of my bishops retreated toward my side because an enemy pawn or knight attacked it, while the opponent gained space or developed a piece.
check: Did one of my pieces retreat recently because an enemy pawn or knight attacked it? If yes, write TREND worse and look first for a forcing central pawn push or a trade of the attacker.

rule: When my king is castled queenside and enemy pieces aim at my 2nd and 3rd rank pawns, guard them (e.g. Bd4, Qe3) before grabbing material.
trigger: My king is castled queenside, and an enemy bishop on a diagonal toward my king or an enemy queen or rook on a half-open file near my king targets the pawns or squares on my 2nd or 3rd rank in front of it.
check: After my move, is every pawn and square in front of my queenside king defended at least as often as the enemy attacks it? If not, play a move that adds a defender there instead.

rule: When an enemy rim knight has no safe squares, attack it immediately with a bishop or pawn, e.g. Bh3, instead of a pawn push elsewhere.
trigger: An enemy knight on the edge of the board has every destination square covered by my pieces or pawns.
check: Is there an enemy rim knight with no safe square that my bishop or pawn can attack right now? If yes, play that attack before any other plan move.

rule: With my king castled queenside, count enemy pieces aimed at the squares in front of it each move; if the count rose, set TREND worse.
trigger: My king is castled on the queenside, and the enemy has pawns advancing on that wing or pieces on the files on or next to my king's file.
check: Do more enemy pieces hit the squares in front of my king than after my last move? If yes, write TREND worse and choose a move that adds a defender to those squares or trades off an attacker, before continuing my own plan.

rule: When my queen pins an enemy knight to its rook, ignore that knight's threats and attack it again, e.g. Bxg5, instead of retreating.
trigger: My queen stands on a line with exactly one enemy piece between it and an enemy rook; that pinned piece attacks one of my pieces, and another of my pieces can attack the pinned piece this move.
check: Is the enemy piece threatening mine pinned to its rook by my queen? If yes, don't retreat: move another piece to attack the pinned piece, taking a loose pawn on the way if possible.

rule: When my rook sits on an enemy bishop's diagonal behind one undefended pawn, move the rook off before trading queens, e.g. Re1.
trigger: One of my rooks stands on a diagonal of an enemy bishop, only one of my pawns stands between them, and that pawn is attacked by the bishop and not defended.
check: If I make my planned move (especially a queen trade or pawn grab), can the enemy bishop take that pawn and then win my rook? If yes, first move the rook off the diagonal to an open file.

rule: In the opening, if my queen has moved repeatedly or retreated without winning material, stop moving it and develop a minor piece or castle.
trigger: Before move 15, my queen has made two or more of my recent moves or just retreated, material is level, and I still have undeveloped minor pieces or an uncastled king.
check: Have I spent two or more recent moves on my queen, or retreated it, without gaining material? If yes, write TREND worse and play a developing or castling move instead of another queen move.
